headlines.h: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders for personal use
headlines.t: Select customers can order the Cybercab at $29,990 plus a $299/month fee; delivery estimated December 2026 in a few Texas cities, geofenced operation only. Musk replied the fee is too high and should be about $115/month.
headlines.why: First steering-wheel-free car sold to consumers: Tesla is testing whether owners will pay for personal unsupervised autonomy.

headlines.h: Cybertruck gets an end date, to make room for Cybercab
headlines.t: Musk said on Nov 6 that Giga Texas would wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027, then on Nov 11 extended it through the end of summer 2027 to work through the backlog. Electrek reports prices rose up to 10% and base Dual Motor orders were paused (cheapest now $92,490).
headlines.why: For a Cybertruck owner: resale and long-term support questions; no statement on support for existing trucks appears in these sources.

headlines.h: Robotaxi: San Antonio launch, bigger Austin, 24/7 everywhere
headlines.t: Tesla launched in San Antonio on Nov 9 (its 8th city, about 273 sq mi vs Waymo's 59). Austin's area grew to about 443 sq mi, and on Nov 11 Tesla said Robotaxi runs 24/7 in every city it serves.
headlines.why: Coverage is now huge on paper, but Axios noted a tracker showed just one Tesla robotaxi in San Antonio at launch.

headlines.h: Texas register: Tesla briefly passed Waymo
headlines.t: Tesla Robotaxi led Waymo 1,302 to 1,297 registered Texas AVs on Nov 10; by early Nov 15 Waymo was back ahead, 1,321 to 1,306.
headlines.why: The best public fleet scorecard shows the two now neck and neck in Texas. Registered does not mean in service.

headlines.h: FSD v14.3.13 keeps rolling; Finland approves it as Tesla Assisted Driving
headlines.t: Build 2026.38.5.13 (Nov 13) carries FSD v14.3.13 with a rewritten MLIR compiler cited for 20% faster reaction time. Finland recognised the Dutch approval on Nov 10; the speed offset is capped at 10% and an EU-wide vote is expected this winter.
headlines.why: This is the software in your truck, and Europe is the next big subscription market.

headlines.h: NHTSA opens a recall query into about 3,000 Waymo vehicles
headlines.t: Regulators want to know why Waymo robotaxis kept passing stopped school buses after a software fix completed in Nov 2025. Separately, ABC7 reported video of a Waymo trying to get around a CHP traffic break on I-280.
headlines.why: The leader's safety record is under fresh review, and it sets the bar for how regulators judge any AV software fix, Tesla's included.

headlines.h: Zoox starts rides in Atlanta and grows in Las Vegas
headlines.t: Employee, family and friends rides began in northwest Atlanta on Nov 13; Las Vegas service expanded to Downtown and the Arts District with 6 a.m.–3 a.m. hours.
headlines.why: The other purpose-built robotaxi (Amazon) is widening its footprint.

headlines.h: Compute: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge, Kakao L4 deal, Wayve on CoreWeave
headlines.t: NVIDIA's 2B-parameter reasoning driving model runs on DRIVE AGX Thor at 160–190 ms pixel-to-trajectory. Kakao Mobility signed an L4 MOU using dual Thor; Wayve signed a multi-year Blackwell training deal with CoreWeave.
headlines.why: NVIDIA is becoming the default car computer and training cloud for the non-Tesla field.

items.t: Cybercab for owners. Buyers must accept delivery in one of a handful of Texas cities; the car runs only in geofenced areas; estimated delivery December 2026; $29,990 plus $299/month. Musk said the fee should be more like $115/month, and Ashok Elluswamy said it will run unsupervised in the same areas as Robotaxi.

Cybertruck wind-down. Nov 6: production at Giga Texas to wind down around mid-2027 for Cybercab. Nov 9: "in about 8 months." Nov 11: extended through end of summer 2027. Electrek estimates a pre-announcement pace of about 30,000 a year and notes no new consumer vehicle has been announced.
San Antonio. Launched Nov 9 with a $16 test ride (vs about $23 on Waymo, per KSAT). Tesla is not yet authorized at the airport, and Axios cited a tracker showing one vehicle at launch.
Hours and area. Austin grew to about 443 sq mi; Robotaxi went 24/7 in all cities on Nov 11, ahead of the year-end goal Tesla gave on its Q3 call.
Fleet. Tesla's Texas register count included 573 Cybercabs and 729 Model Ys when it passed Waymo on Nov 10.

FSD v14.3.13 notes: upgraded RL training, new vision encoder, MLIR compiler for 20% faster reaction, better handling of emergency vehicles, school buses and small animals, and an intervention-free streak counter.

Subscriptions. Not a Tesla App reports, citing a source, that Musk personally decided to drop basic Autopilot from new cars to boost FSD subscriptions; Tesla reported a record 1.74M subscribers in Q3.
Europe. In Finland the system is now Tesla Assisted Driving, max speed offset 10% and reset each drive. Build 2026.39.100 (FSD 14.2.2.7) brings the renaming to Europe.
China. Electrek reports Tesla's domestic retail sales there fell 66% in October.
Waymo: NHTSA's recall query covers nearly 3,000 vehicles; Austin ISD documented 19 violations. Waymo says it has had no citations since March.
Waymo: a driverless car tried twice to pass a CHP traffic break on I-280 near John Daly Blvd before officers blocked it.
Waymo: South Bay expansion takes the Bay Area area to 350 sq mi; it also offers $2.85 credits for pairing rides with transit.
Zoox: Atlanta rides for employees, family and friends; public Explorers program planned there in 2027. Las Vegas: Downtown, Arts District, 6 a.m.–3 a.m.
Pony.ai: mapping Manchester with Uber and Verne, safety drivers and no passengers; no passenger application yet.
Rivian: CEO RJ Scaringe calls 2027 an inflection year; point-to-point driving is coming first to employees, then customers, with AVs on Uber targeted by 2028.
GM: Super Cruise launches in Europe in mid-December on the Optiq, Lyriq and Vistiq, across 111,000+ miles in 16 countries.
Mercedes: CTO Jörg Burzer frames the hand-on-wheel city rule as the L2/L3 line; FSD users interviewed by InsideEVs were unconvinced.
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge: 2B-parameter reasoning VLA that reasons only when needed; closed-loop RL improved driving 48.9%; 160–190 ms on DRIVE AGX Thor.
Kakao Mobility × NVIDIA: L4 MOU with two DRIVE AGX Thor units, Hyperion and Halos, starting on Kia PBVs; no deployment timeline set.
Wayve × CoreWeave: multi-year deal on Blackwell GPUs for training, evaluation and simulation.
Huawei: second Qiankun open contest closed Nov 13 with 190,000+ owners; ADS 5 adds roaming cruise assist and rear-collision avoidance.
BYD: 4.19M+ cars with driver assistance and 260M km of data a day (up from 3.95M at end-September).
BYD Seal 07 (God's Eye B, lidar plus one Orin X) demonstrated emergency steering at 130 km/h; Denza launched the N8 on Nov 12 with God's Eye B.
Li Auto: OTA 9.2 brings Mach VLA 2.5 with a 3D ViT perception model, such as reversing to yield on narrow roads.
NHTSA extended comments to Dec 10 on FMVSS 108 changes for vehicles without manual controls, including optional cyan ADS marker lamps.
Texas liability: a lawyer told KSAT that with no human intervention the company generally stands in the shoes of the operator; Tesla's terms include arbitration.
Finland approval is national; the EU-wide decision needs a TCMV vote, then about three weeks to take effect.
Tesla: 2026.38.5.13 (Nov 13, North America) and 2026.39.100 (Nov 11, Europe).
GM: OnStar AI Assistant premieres on the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq and can control vehicle functions; GM expects $10.5B in software and services revenue this year.
Li Auto OTA 9.2 also adds a map-trip agent and CarPlay/HiCar connectivity.
Wayve–CoreWeave compute deal and Kakao–NVIDIA L4 MOU (both Nov 9).
Lemonade expanded its FSD insurance discount (50% off FSD miles) to Ohio.
Just before the window: Neolix raised nearly $400M (Nov 2), Humble Robotics $51M (Nov 5).

before.t: Baidu unveiled the Apollo World simulator (Nov 3).
XPeng got citywide L4 demo approval in Guangzhou; CEO expects L4 deployment around late 2028.
VW China launched in-house HS8 L2++ and holds an L3 test permit in Hefei.
BMW: navigation-guided city L2 in Germany from 2027.
Qualcomm and Infineon paired safety MCUs with Snapdragon Ride.

analysis: Tesla is moving from selling cars to selling autonomy: Cybercab pre-orders plus the Cybertruck end date make that explicit.
Its robotaxi footprint is growing fastest on paper, but service areas are outrunning vehicles in new cities; Waymo still leads on cities and fleet.
Waymo's school-bus query shows regulators will judge AV software fixes by real-world results, which applies to every driverless operator, Tesla included.
Outside Tesla, NVIDIA is consolidating the stack: in-car compute (Thor), models (Alpamayo) and training cloud partners.
